Name:  ___                  Unit No:   ___
 
Admission Date:  ___              Discharge Date:   ___
 
Date of Birth:  ___             Sex:   F
 
Service: SURGERY
 
Allergies: 
Patient recorded as having No Known Allergies to Drugs
 
Attending: ___.
 
Chief Complaint:
morbid obesity
 
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:
1. Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass.
2. Endoscopy.

 
History of Present Illness:
___ has class III morbid obesity with weight of 230.8 pounds
as of ___ (her initial screen weight on ___ was 232.3
pounds), height of 64 inches and BMI of 40.  Her previous weight
loss efforts have included Weight Watchers and Slim-Fast.  She
has lost up to 20 pounds but was unable to maintain weight for
any significant length of time.  She has not taking prescription
weight loss medications or used over-the-counter
ephedra-containing appetite suppressant/herbal supplements.  She
has had weight issues for the past ___ years and cites as factors
contributing to her excess weight lunch portions, too many
carbohydrates, grazing, and emotional eating and lack of
exercise.  She recently started ___ for one hour 2 to 3 days
per week for activity
 
Past Medical History:
PMH

2. gastroesophageal reflux
3. polycystic ovary syndrome
4. fatty liver
PSH

2. shoulder surgery in ___
3. tubal ligation in ___

 
Social History:
___
Family History:
Her family history remarkable for obesity and CAD
 
Physical Exam:
Blood pressure was 110/74, pulse 78, respirations 16 and O2
saturation 98% on room air.  On physical examination ___ was
casually dressed, affect was flat somewhat and she was in no
distress.  Her skin was warm, dry with no rashes, there were
tattoos on her left breast and right foot. Sclerae were
anicteric, conjunctiva clear, pupils were equal round and
reactive to light, fundi were normal, mucous membranes were
moist, tongue was pink and the oropharynx was without exudates 
or
hyperemia.  Trachea was in the midline and the neck was supple
with no adenopathy, thyromegaly or carotid bruits.  Chest was
symmetric and the lungs were clear to auscultation bilaterally
with good air movement.  Cardiac exam was regular rate and 
rhythm
with normal S1 and S2, no murmurs, rubs or gallops.  The abdomen
was obese but soft and non-tender, non-distended with positive
bowel sounds and no masses or hernias, there were no incision
scars.  There is no spinal tenderness or flank pain.  Lower
extremities were without edema, venous stasis or clubbing,
perfusion was good.  There was no evidence of joint swelling or
inflammation of the joints.  There were no focal neurological
deficits and her gait was normal
 
Pertinent Results:
___ 03:02PM   HCT-38.3

___ UGI :  Status post gastric bypass with no evidence of 
obstruction or leak. 

 
Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ was admitted to the hospital and taken to the 
Operating Room where she underwent a laparoscopic gastric 
bypass.  She tolerated the procedure well and returned to the 
PACU in stable condition.  She maintained stable hemodynamics 
and her pain was well controlled with a Dilaudid PCA.
Following transfer to the Surgical floor she continued to make 
good progress.  She had an upper GI on ___ which confirmed 
no anastomotic leak and she began a stage 1 diet.  Over the next 
___ hours her diet was gradually advanced to stage 3 which she 
tolerated well.  Her pain was well controlled with oral Roxicet 
and she was up and walking independently.  Her port sites were 
dry and her JP drain was  removed without difficulty.  After an 
uneventful recovery she was discharged on ___ and will 
follow up with Dr. ___ in 2 weeks.

Discharge Disposition:
Home
 
Discharge Diagnosis:
1. Obstructive sleep apnea.
2. Morbid obesity.
3. Gastroesophageal reflux.

 
Discharge Condition:
Mental Status: Clear and coherent.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Ambulatory - Independent.

 
Discharge Instructions:
Discharge Instructions: Please call your surgeon or return to 
the emergency department if you develop a fever greater than 
101.5, chest pain, shortness of breath, severe abdominal pain, 
pain unrelieved by your pain medication, severe nausea or 
vomiting, severe abdominal bloating, inability to eat or drink, 
foul smelling or colorful drainage from your incisions, redness 
or swelling around your incisions, or any other symptoms which 
are concerning to you.

Diet: Stay on Stage III diet until your follow up appointment. 
Do not self advance
diet, do not drink out of a straw or chew gum.

Medication Instructions:
Resume your home medications, CRUSH ALL PILLS.
You will be starting some new medications:
1.  You are being discharged on medications to treat the pain 
from your operation. These medications will make you drowsy and 
impair your ability to drive a motor vehicle or operate 
machinery safely. You MUST refrain from such activities while 
taking these medications.
2. You should begin taking a chewable complete multivitamin with 
minerals. No gummy vitamins.
3. You will be taking Zantac liquid ___ mg twice daily for one 
month. This medicine prevents gastric reflux.
4. You will be taking Actigall 300 mg twice daily for 6 months. 
This medicine prevents you from having problems with your 
gallbladder.
5. You should take a stool softener, Colace, twice daily for 
constipation as needed, or until you resume a normal bowel 
pattern.
6. You must not use NSAIDS (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory 
drugs) Examples are Ibuprofen, Motrin, Aleve, Nuprin and 
Naproxen. These agents will cause bleeding and ulcers in your 
digestive system.

Activity:
No heavy lifting of items ___ pounds for 6 weeks. You may 
resume moderate
exercise at your discretion, no abdominal exercises.

Wound Care:
You may shower, no tub baths or swimming. 
If there is clear drainage from your incisions, cover with 
clean, dry gauze. 
Your steri-strips will fall off on their own. Please remove any 
remaining strips ___ days after surgery.
Please call the doctor if you have increased pain, swelling, 
redness, or drainage from the incision sites. 

 
Followup Instructions:
___

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with morbid obesity and esophageal dysmotility,
status post gastric bypass.

SINGLE CONTRAST UPPER GI SERIES:  Scout views demonstrate no free air under
the diaphragm.  A drain is noted within the left upper quadrant.  Surgical
clips are seen along the left mid abdomen.  Due to table restrictions related
to weight, the exam was performed only in the upright position.  Water-soluble
contrast followed by thin barium was used in the study.  Contrast was noted to
pass freely through the esophagus filling the included portion of the stomach
with prompt emptying into the jejunum at the site of gastrojejunal
anastomosis.  There is no evidence of dehiscence or escape of barium into the
excluded stomach.

IMPRESSION:  Status post gastric bypass with no evidence of obstruction or
leak. Findings discussed with ___ at 11:21pm on ___.
